author: Contributor 79
about: Replay the registry reference response examples, preserving the published samples. Setup publishes their real tarballs with the manifest fields the examples show; revisions, timestamps and digests are vendor generated and compared by type rather than pinned. The authentication page's rule that credentials come in Basic or Bearer form is replayed on a restricted package the page's own account (username, password) publishes: the right password reads it, a wrong one publishes nothing.

steps.name: The documentation examples run on a synthetic registry account
Publish tiny-tarball@1.0.0 so the documented read has its subject

body.name: tiny-tarball
body.description: tiny tarball used for health checks
body.readme:
# TinyTarball

tiny-tarball used for health checks

**don't unpublish me!**

1.0.0.description: tiny tarball used for health checks
1.0.0.name: tiny-tarball

expect.equals:
# TinyTarball

tiny-tarball used for health checks

**don't unpublish me!**
tiny tarball used for health checks
tiny tarball used for health checks

body.name: yargs
body.description: yargs the modern, pirate-themed, successor to optimist.

6.6.0.name: yargs
6.6.0.description: yargs the modern, pirate-themed, successor to optimist.

steps.name: The authentication page's examples sign in as `username` with `password`: the account, made on npmjs.com's sign-up page
username publishes @username/private-package 1.0.0 without --access public, so it is restricted to them
